$comment: Rule catalog — integrity. Standards 3, 15, 19. Every entry here is a non-exemptible prohibition against presenting something as measured that was not. They share one criterion: an approved exception would amount to written permission to deceive, and no project circumstance changes that. None of them is machine-checkable — nothing in a repository distinguishes a real number from an invented one — so all three report not-evaluated and are satisfied, if at all, by attestation.

rules.title: Data that was not collected is not presented as collected
rules.description: Records that were not obtained must not be presented as observations. This covers inventing rows outright and the quieter forms: describing synthetic or simulated data as observed, filling gaps by generation without disclosure, and reporting a dataset size that includes rows never collected.
rules.rationale: Every downstream conclusion inherits the claim that the data describes the world. Synthetic data is legitimate and often necessary — what makes it fabrication is the description rather than the generation, and the description is what travels.
rules.remediation: Label synthetic or simulated data as such wherever the dataset is described, and correct any reported size or coverage figure that counted generated records as collected ones.
rules.evidenceExpected: An attestation from someone who traced the dataset to its collection mechanism, naming what they checked and confirming that every record described as observed was obtained rather than generated.
rules.$assuranceNote: Nothing automated establishes this. A scan cannot distinguish a measured value from an invented one, and a passing result would assert exactly the thing it cannot see.
rules.$exemptibilityNote: Non-exemptible. An approved exception permitting fabricated data is written permission to deceive. The legitimate neighbouring act — using synthetic data and saying so — requires no exception because it violates nothing.

rules.title: Training results that were not produced are not reported
rules.description: A training result must correspond to a run that happened. This prohibits inventing figures, and equally prohibits reporting a number from one configuration as though it came from another, carrying forward a stale result after the code changed, and presenting an expected outcome as an observed one.
rules.rationale: A fabricated training result is undetectable downstream and propagates into every comparison, every decision to ship, and every claim about the model. The stale-carry-forward case is the common one and rarely feels like fabrication while producing the same falsehood.
rules.remediation: Re-run the configuration and report what it produced, or withdraw the figure. Where a number is an expectation rather than a measurement, say so in the place it is reported.
rules.evidenceExpected: An attestation that reported training figures were traced to the runs that produced them, naming the run records or experiment-tracking entries examined.
rules.$assuranceNote: Nothing automated establishes this. Re-running the target project's training to verify a figure was considered and rejected: executing the code under audit is outside this tool's contract, and a partial rerun that agrees in a different environment would be worse than no check.
rules.$exemptibilityNote: Non-exemptible. An exception to fabricating results is an oxymoron; there is no project circumstance under which reporting a number nobody measured becomes acceptable.

rules.title: Evaluation metrics that were not measured are not reported
rules.description: A reported evaluation metric must be the output of an evaluation that was run, on the data and split it is said to describe. This prohibits inventing figures, and also reporting a validation number as a test number, quoting a figure from a different split, and rounding in a direction chosen after seeing which side of a threshold it fell.
rules.rationale: Evaluation metrics are the evidence on which a model is accepted, compared, and deployed. A fabricated one does not merely misstate performance; it removes the only signal that would have caught the model being wrong.
rules.remediation: Re-run the evaluation on the stated data and split, and report what it produced. Where a figure came from a different split than the one it is presented under, correct the attribution.
rules.evidenceExpected: An attestation that reported metrics were traced to the evaluation runs and splits they claim, naming the records examined.
rules.$assuranceNote: Nothing automated establishes this. A repository contains numbers and code; it does not contain the fact that a particular number came from running that code.
rules.$exemptibilityNote: Non-exemptible. An approved exception here would sanction publishing evidence that does not exist, which is the failure the entire evaluation half of this framework is built to prevent.
